answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded stake with slashing. Each agent locks collateral into a shared atlas of registered identities before acting, and peer attestations build slowly, so trust forms like a pearl instead of appearing instantly. When validators detect coordinated fake personas, their bonds are slashed and burned and reputation resets to zero. Each fake identity therefore requires real locked capital, and scaling bonds with persona count makes mass attacks unaffordable: the registry replaces an ivory tower of anonymous accounts with priced, slashable risk.
